data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's distinguishing evidence (divergence-stratum advantage) fails to separate genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that tracks the right answer. The target argues the benefit must concentrate where the checklist's indicated action diverges from the panel's default, treating divergence-stratum advantage as evidence of genuine information content. But if the checklist encodes a decision rule that happens to track the right answer without the panel understanding WHY, divergence cases are exactly where rote compliance produces the largest apparent improvement — the panel follows an alien rule it would not have used, precisely because the rule says so, not because it has acquired genuine reliability. The target's own overturn condition admits the divergence stratum is confounded by difficulty (all hard cases are divergence cases), but it does not resolve this confound: a compliance-driven panel could show its entire advantage in the divergence stratum simply because that is where following instructions matters most. Thus the 'divergence-stratum advantage' observable cannot distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance that happens to track the right answer, which is exactly what the problem demands the evidence do.
